title: Database schema for the domain model
user_visible_behavior: Running db/schema.sql creates tables for users, tokens, work orders, status history, typologies L1/L2/L3 (L3 with default priority), locations, location types and the AI Prefill log.
verification: Schema script runs twice on MariaDB without errors (idempotent or drop-and-create)
Foreign keys enforce L3→L2→L1 parents, work order→location/typology/users
notes: Source: docs/domain-model.md. Users have an is_service_account flag. Status and priority values in Spanish per CONTEXT.md.

title: Realistic seed data for one hotel
user_visible_behavior: Running db/seed.sql loads location types, a flat list of hotel locations, a typology tree with default priorities, a few technicians and the MCP service account.
verification: Seed loads after schema without errors
Query confirms every L3 has a default priority and every location has a type
Passwords are stored as password_hash values
notes: Open question: who authors the realistic typology tree. Seed must support the evaluation scenarios (room numbers, Piscina, named technicians, duplicate first names).

title: API router accepts only POST JSON requests
user_visible_behavior: Requests to /api/<endpoint> are routed by name; non-POST methods and unknown endpoints get a consistent JSON error with the right HTTP status.
verification: curl GET returns 405 JSON error; unknown endpoint returns 404 JSON error
Test script covers both cases
notes: No framework. Define the single error response shape here and reuse it everywhere.

title: User logs in and receives a token
user_visible_behavior: POST /login with valid username and password returns a random token with an expiry; wrong credentials return a 401 JSON error.
verification: Test: valid seed credentials return a token stored server-side with expiry
Test: wrong password returns 401 and creates no token
notes: Initial stance: 8h lifetime, no refresh. Never log passwords.

title: Protected endpoints reject missing or expired tokens
user_visible_behavior: Any endpoint except /login returns 401 JSON when the token is missing, unknown or expired, and receives the authenticated user when valid.
verification: Tests for missing, unknown, expired and valid tokens against a protected test endpoint
notes: Service-account tokens are limited to the read endpoints the MCP needs (docs/technical-discovery.md).

title: Location catalog endpoints return seeded locations
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-location-types and POST /get-locations return the seeded types and locations (each with its type) for an authenticated user.
verification: Test: both endpoints return seed data with a valid token and 401 without
notes: Flat list, one hotel.

title: Typology endpoints return each level filtered by parent
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-level-1-typologies returns all L1; /get-level-2-typologies and /get-level-3-typologies return children of a given parent id, with L3 including its default priority.
verification: Test: L2 filtered by L1 id and L3 filtered by L2 id match seed data
Test: unknown parent id returns an empty list or a validation error consistently
notes: Used by the cascading selects and by the MCP tools.

title: Assignable users endpoint excludes service accounts
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-users returns users (id, first name, last names) that can be assignees; service accounts never appear.
verification: Test: seeded technicians are returned, the MCP service account is not
notes: Needed by the assignee select and the MCP; pulled into the MVP although the brief listed it as low priority.

title: Create a validated work order with initial status history
user_visible_behavior: POST /create-work-order saves a work order with creator from the token, validated location/L3 typology/assignee, priority (L3 default unless provided), status Asignado if assigned else Pendiente, and writes the first status history entry.
verification: Test: with assignee → Asignado; without → Pendiente; one history entry each
Test: unknown location/typology/user ids or a service-account assignee are rejected
Test: omitted priority falls back to the L3 default, provided priority is kept
notes: L1/L2 are derived from L3 (docs/domain-model.md).

title: List work orders newest first
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-work-orders returns work orders with location, L3 typology, status, priority, assignee name and creation date, newest first.
verification: Test: created orders appear newest first with resolved display names
notes: Pagination/filtering not required for the PoC.

title: Read one work order with its status history
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-work-order returns all fields of one work order including L1/L2/L3, creator, assignee, full description and the ordered status history.
verification: Test: returns full detail and history for an existing id; 404 JSON for unknown id

title: Dashboard summary counts work orders
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-work-orders-summary returns the count of work orders per status (all five, zeros included) and the count of open (not Resuelto/Cancelado) work orders per priority (Alta, Media, Baja).
verification: Test: after creating orders in known statuses/priorities, counts match; statuses and priorities with no orders return 0
Test: closed orders are excluded from the priority counts
notes: Feeds the dashboard home screen (MVP).

title: Spike: tool calling round-trips on both LLM providers
user_visible_behavior: A throwaway PHP script sends one Anthropic Messages request with a tool definition to the Anthropic API and to DevExpert inference, returns a tool_result, and prints the final answer.
verification: Script output saved as evidence for each provider: tool_use received, tool_result accepted, final text returned
Result (works / fails / caveats) recorded in docs/risks-and-open-questions.md
notes: Highest risk: tool calling is undocumented on DevExpert (docs/risks-and-open-questions.md). Uses cURL only. Consumes DevExpert quota.

title: Spike: PHP drives a stdio child process on XAMPP Windows
user_visible_behavior: A throwaway PHP script starts a child PHP process with proc_open, exchanges newline-delimited JSON messages over stdin/stdout, and shuts it down cleanly with no orphan process.
verification: Script run on XAMPP PHP exchanges 3 request/response pairs and exits; Task Manager shows no leftover php.exe
notes: Risk: Windows pipe buffering and blocking reads. Findings recorded in docs/risks-and-open-questions.md.

title: MCP server completes initialize and lists tools
user_visible_behavior: Running `php mcp/server.php` with the correct MCP API key answers initialize and tools/list over stdio JSON-RPC; with a missing or wrong key it exits with an error.
verification: Test pipes initialize + tools/list into the server and checks the JSON-RPC responses
Test: wrong key exits non-zero without serving
notes: No libraries. Key passed via environment variable by the connector (ADR 0001).

title: MCP tools return hotel data through the API
user_visible_behavior: tools/call for list locations, list typologies (by level and parent) and list assignable users returns data fetched from the API with the service-account login.
verification: Test pipes tools/call requests and compares results with seed data
Test: no write tool is exposed
notes: Read-only. A work-order read tool is optional for the PoC.

title: Configurable Anthropic Messages provider adapter
user_visible_behavior: The AI connector sends a Messages request (with tools) to the provider selected in config (base URL, key, model) and returns parsed content blocks; switching provider requires only a config change.
verification: Test with a stubbed HTTP transport: request shape and headers match the Messages format; tool_use blocks are parsed
Manual: one real call per configured provider succeeds
notes: Behind a provider interface so an OpenAI-compatible adapter can be added later. Never log keys.

title: Agent loop relays tool calls between LLM and MCP
user_visible_behavior: Given a description and the creator's identity, the connector starts the MCP server, offers its tools to the LLM, relays tool calls until a final JSON answer (location, L1/L2/L3, assignee, notes) or the iteration cap, then stops the MCP process.
verification: Test with a stubbed LLM that issues two tool calls then a final answer: MCP is called and the answer is returned
Test: iteration cap returns a controlled error and the MCP process is terminated
notes: ADR 0001. Assignee only when named or self-assigned ('asígnamelo'); priority is not inferred.

title: Inference endpoint returns validated prefill with notes
user_visible_behavior: POST /get-work-order-inference returns suggested location, L1/L2/L3, priority (from L3 default) and assignee; invalid, inconsistent or service-account values are blanked with a prefill note, and the run is written to the AI Prefill log.
verification: Test with stubbed loop output containing a bad location id and an L3 not under its L2: both blanked with notes
Manual: real call with 'El aire de la 214 no enfría, asígnamelo' returns the expected fields and a log row
notes: Zero invalid IDs reach the frontend (success criterion).

title: Evaluation script measures prefill accuracy and latency
user_visible_behavior: Running the evaluation script sends ~20 Spanish sample descriptions to the inference endpoint and reports per-field accuracy, invalid-ID count and latency per sample.
verification: Report saved as evidence for each provider; targets: ≥80% fields correct, 0 invalid IDs, ~≤15 s per prefill
notes: Samples cover self-assignment, named technician, ambiguous name, unknown room, ambiguous typology. Consumes DevExpert quota.

title: Login screen stores the token and opens the app
user_visible_behavior: On a 360px screen the user enters username and password, sees an error on bad credentials, and on success lands on the home screen (dashboard once ui-dashboard is built, a placeholder before that).
verification: Manual in browser at 360px: bad and good credentials behave as described
Opening an app page without a valid token redirects to login
notes: DESIGN.md. UI copy in Spanish.

title: Collapsible side menu navigation
user_visible_behavior: Authenticated pages show a top bar and a side menu (hidden on mobile, persistent at ≥993px) linking to the dashboard, the list, new manual work order and new AI work order.
verification: Manual at 360px and 1200px: menu toggles on mobile and stays open on desktop; links navigate
notes: W3.CSS w3-sidebar; minimal JS. Logout link added by ui-logout.

title: Dashboard home with status and priority counts
user_visible_behavior: After login the user lands on the dashboard, which shows one tile per status with its count and one tile per priority counting open work orders; the side menu links back to it.
verification: Manual at 360px: tiles match the API response; login lands here; menu link works
notes: DESIGN.md core screen 2. No floating AI button (list screen only).

title: Work order list with floating AI button
user_visible_behavior: The list shows work order cards (location, L3, status and priority tags, assignee, date) and a floating AI button that opens AI creation; tapping a card opens its detail.
verification: Manual at 360px with seeded/created orders: cards render, FAB visible only on this screen and navigates to AI creation
notes: FAB on the list screen only (DESIGN.md).

title: Work order detail with status history
user_visible_behavior: The detail screen shows all work order fields, the full description and the status history in order.
verification: Manual: open a created order from the list and compare with the API response
notes: No FAB here.

title: Manual work order form with cascading typologies
user_visible_behavior: The user writes a description, picks a location, L1→L2→L3 (priority fills from the L3 default and can be changed) and an optional assignee, saves, and sees the new order in the list.
verification: Manual at 360px: changing L1 resets L2/L3; choosing L3 sets priority; saving shows the order with the correct status
notes: The form is reused by the AI flow and by edit. DESIGN.md core screen 5b (Stitch 05-new-work-order.png): dialog form, no status field on create, no attachments.

title: AI creation prefills the form for review
user_visible_behavior: The user writes a description and requests AI Prefill; a loading state shows 'Analizando…'; the form is then filled with highlighted AI fields and prefill notes on blank fields; the user adjusts and saves.
verification: Manual end-to-end MVP walkthrough at 360px: login → dashboard → list → FAB → description → prefill → review → save → order visible in list and detail
Manual: unknown room shows a blank location with a note
notes: Completes the MVP slice in docs/build-brief.md. DESIGN.md core screen 5a (Stitch 05-new-work-order-with-ai.png): description dialog with Enviar, then the 5b form prefilled.

title: Update a work order enforcing lifecycle rules
user_visible_behavior: POST /update-work-order changes editable fields and status following the guided lifecycle; closed orders are rejected; each status change writes a history entry.
verification: Tests: assign→Asignado, unassign→Pendiente, En resolución requires assignee, Resuelto only from En resolución, Cancelado from any open status, closed orders not editable, history written on each change
notes: Post-MVP-slice. Initial stance: creator, created at and description are not editable (open question).

title: Edit work order screen
user_visible_behavior: From the detail, the user edits an open work order (fields and status) and sees the result; closed orders are shown read-only.
verification: Manual at 360px: edit status and assignee of an open order; closed order offers no edit
notes: Only valid next statuses are offered. DESIGN.md core screen 6: no Stitch screen; reuses the 5b form titled Editar parte.

title: Logout revokes the token
user_visible_behavior: POST /logout invalidates the current token; later requests with it get 401.
verification: Test: token works before logout and returns 401 after
notes: Low priority.

title: Logout from the side menu
user_visible_behavior: Choosing logout in the side menu revokes the token and returns to the login screen.
verification: Manual: after logout, the back button cannot reach app pages without logging in
